newsitem.title: USA: Great Western holders approve merger.
newsitem.headline: Great Western holders approve merger.

text.p: Great Western Financial Corp shareholders approved the $6.9 billion merger with Washington Mutual Inc on Friday.

At a special meeting here, 98 percent of the voting shareholders approved the deal, which would create the nation's largest thrift. Washington Mutual shareholders are expected to vote on the deal at a separate meeting later today.
The vote came a little more than a week after H.F. Ahmanson and Co dropped its hostile bid for Great Western, ending a bitter savings-and-loan takeover battle.

Ahmanson initially launched its offer in February. Great Western, based in Chatsworth, Calif., rejected the bid and on March 6 announced it agreed to be bought by Washington Mutual in a deal that would create the largest U.S. thrift, with $86 billion in assets.
After trying unsuccessfully to persuade shareholders to support its bid, Ahmanson withdrew its offer on June 4.
